summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (JTM 1.5/12)

data.turoyo: U ǧloyo i maʕnayḏe, u səfoqo d əṯewo, manḍafwole mu ʕaǧaq, mu wasax d lə foyəš aʕle, w nufaqwo u ṣəfərayḏe d lo wasax d foyəš, lašan d mosək darmono w d mibayəḏ̣.
data.translation: Waschen bedeutet ... wenn ein Stück Geschirr ankam, reinigte man es von dem Dreck, von dem Schmutz, damit er nicht daran haften blieb, damit sein Kupfer zum Vorschein kam und ohne Schmutz war, damit es das Mittel annahm und sich verzinnen ließ.

rationale: First I Infinitiv/1 example; the text explicitly defines the cleaning operation before tinning.

summary: New box Part act.: example for sense 1 in Part act. (MAC Hanna Dewo/214)

data.turoyo: ḤD. E, maǧbúr! Ḥa+mbayḏono, ŭ ḥa+ǧaloyo ŭ ḥa+nafoḥo.
data.translation: Yes, it’s necessary! One tinsmith, one polisher, and one blower.

rationale: First I Part act./1 example, provisionally including the substantivised craft agent ǧaloyo; its polishing role is explicit in a parallel list of workers.

summary: The new action noun and occupational agent refer to I cleaning/polishing, not II trilling. The craft context links cleaning to exposing copper before it accepts tinning material.

The old and new Prym–Socin witnesses use different citation systems (prs 234/26 versus PrS 80/86) and different ž/ǧ spelling. Their identical clause establishes a parallel passage, not a demonstrated citation error.
MAC Hanna Dewo/214: should the lexical occupational noun ǧaloyo be retained among substantivised Part act. forms? It is provisionally included there rather than treated as a new simple-verb sense.
Confirm the mapping of prs 234/26 page/line to PrS 80/86 text/verse before changing the existing reference.
